Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Serve as the Technical Director responsible to the Commander for the technical control, coordination and management of the facility's programs with maximum delegation of technical and administrative management matters. Provide extensive input and influence in development of the guiding policies, philosophies and objectives of operations
Details.SubAgencyName: Yuma Proving Ground Office of the Commander
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. The U.S. Army Yuma Proving Ground (YPG) is the Army's premier test center featuring the longest overland artillery range in the nation. YPG conducts developmental testing on nearly every piece of equipment in the ground combat arsenal. The proving ground is at the forefront of Army modernization efforts, actively supporting six of the Army Futures Command's cross-functional teams building the future force. YPG is the host site of the annual Project Convergence capstone event, the largest capabilities demonstration in the Army.
MajorDuties: Serves as Technical Director and is responsible to the Commander for accomplishment of the total mission and the effective and economical internal functioning of the organization.
Responsible to the Commander for the technical control, coordination and management of the facility's programs with maximum delegation of technical and administrative management matters.
As the senior civilian authority, provides direction, guidance, oversight, and supervision for all activities of the command.
Manages program planning for life cycle test capabilities.
Directs strategic planning to ensure test capabilities are ready and relevant to support scheduled tests.
Assures professional development of test personnel to become subject matter experts in their respective fields.
Advances testing methodology and technology plans, studies, programs and policies to efficiently and effectively test complex weapon system technologies.
Maintains viable safety, environmental and security programs and complies with governing policies and regulations.
Oversees the management of resources, schedules and budgets in all phases of operations.

Participates and represents the organization in conferences and meetings that requires extensive preparation to exchange information, evaluate and coordinate projects, defend actions, and propose controversial solutions.
Works with management to establish new fundamental concepts and criteria and stimulate the development of new policies, methodologies and techniques.

One year of specialized experience at the GS-11 or equivalent performing the following duties: Serve as the Information Systems coordinator for all Managers, System Administrators and End Users in resolving complex day-to-day computer hardware and software failures. Install new hardware and software, write minor batch files, set up program menus, and make minor hardware and software modifications and test systems to ensure optimum operation to fill end user requirements. Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. 2. Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. 3. Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. 4. Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations.
